question: When creating 10 mm single-stroke capital letters in vertical style, what does the 10 mm distance between horizontal parallel lines represent?
solution:
The correct answer is __Letter height**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Letter height__ is defined as the distance between the top and bottom horizontal parallel lines of a letter.
 
• In engineering drawing, the letter height determines the overall size of the text that is used for annotations and dimensions.
 
• For single-stroke capital letters, the height is consistent across all characters.
 
• The standard height ensures uniformity and readability in technical drawings.
 
• Using 10 mm for letter height is a common practice when creating vertical-style single-stroke capital letters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Letter Width:**

 
 
• It refers to the horizontal size of a letter but is not represented by the 10 mm distance.
 
 
 
• **Interline Spacing:**
 
 
• Interline spacing refers to the vertical distance between two lines of text, which is different from letter height.
 
 
 
• **Stroke Thickness:**
 
 
• It refers to the width of the line used to create the letters, which is much smaller than the letter height.
